name: 5 Division (Makurdi) — new
summary: New divisional HQ approved July 2026 for Benue, Nasarawa and Kogi states.
description: 5 Division is one of four divisional headquarters created when President Bola Tinubu approved the Nigerian Army's expansion from eight to twelve divisions on 23 July 2026. Headquartered in Makurdi, it takes over responsibility for Benue, Nasarawa and Kogi states from 3 Division and previously uncommitted forces in the North-Central theatre. The Army states that the division will commence operations on attaining Initial Operational Capability and progress towards Full Operational Capability.
statusDetail: Approved by the President on 23 July 2026 and announced by the Presidency. A General Officer Commanding was appointed on 30 July 2026. It forms part of Phase 1 of the new force structure, which the Army expects to complete by September 2026. Operations begin on attaining Initial Operational Capability (IOC), with Full Operational Capability (FOC) to follow.
mouSigned: Not applicable — a military formation, not a commercial project
mouParties: Federal Government of Nigeria (Presidency and Ministry of Defence); Nigerian Army
mouSignificance: Creation approved by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu on 23 July 2026, announced by the President's Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga. The division is commanded by a General Officer Commanding appointed by the Chief of Army Staff, Lt.-Gen. Waidi Shaibu.

milestones.event: President Tinubu approves the expansion of the Nigerian Army from eight to twelve divisions, including a new divisional headquarters in Makurdi.
Benue State Government confirms approval of the 5 Division Headquarters in Makurdi.
Army appoints a General Officer Commanding for 5 Division.
Phase 1 target: 5, 9 and 10 Divisions established and existing formations reorganised.

phase: Phase 1 of two (targeted complete by September 2026)
aorNote: Benue, Nasarawa and Kogi states. Benue, Nasarawa and Kogi are carved out of the former 3 Division (Jos) North-Central area of responsibility.
significance: Restores a dedicated divisional headquarters for the North-Central states and cuts response time for the Benue Valley and Niger-Benue corridor.

name: 9 Division (Ilorin) — new
type: New Nigerian Army divisional headquarters (Kwara and Niger)
summary: New divisional HQ approved July 2026 covering Kwara and Niger states.
description: 9 Division is a new Nigerian Army divisional headquarters headquartered in Ilorin, Kwara State, created under the Army's expansion to twelve divisions approved on 23 July 2026. It assumes responsibility for Kwara and Niger states — a band that includes the disputed Niger–Kwara boundary area and the corridor along the Niger River system into the Sahel. The division falls in Phase 1 of the restructuring.
statusDetail: Approved by the President on 23 July 2026 and announced by the Presidency. A General Officer Commanding was appointed on 30 July 2026. It is part of Phase 1 of the new force structure, targeted for completion by September 2026. The Army has not published its formation type or detailed unit composition.
mouSigned: Not applicable — a military formation, not a commercial project
mouParties: Federal Government of Nigeria (Presidency and Ministry of Defence); Nigerian Army
mouSignificance: Creation approved by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu on 23 July 2026, announced by Bayo Onanuga. Local support was expressed by the Ilorin Emirate Descendants Progressive Union. A General Officer Commanding was appointed by the Chief of Army Staff on 30 July 2026.

milestones.event: President Tinubu approves creation of the 9 Division headquarters in Ilorin, Kwara State.
Ilorin Emirate Descendants Progressive Union publicly welcomes the new division.
Army appoints a General Officer Commanding for 9 Division.
Phase 1 target: division established and operational.

phase: Phase 1 of two (targeted complete by September 2026)
aorNote: Kwara and Niger states, covering the Niger–Kwara belt and the middle Niger corridor.
significance: Fills a divisional gap in the middle belt, improving command coverage for Kwara and Niger states.

name: 10 Division (Jalingo) — new
type: New Nigerian Army divisional headquarters (North-East and North-Central)
summary: New divisional HQ approved July 2026 for Taraba and Adamawa states.
description: 10 Division is a new Nigerian Army divisional headquarters headquartered in Jalingo, Taraba State, created under the expansion to twelve divisions approved on 23 July 2026. It assumes responsibility for Taraba and Adamawa states, absorbing the two states that were previously part of 7 Division (Maiduguri) area of responsibility. Its creation places a divisional headquarters on the road and rail corridor between the Benue Valley and the Mambilla Plateau.
statusDetail: Approved by the President on 23 July 2026 and announced by the Presidency. A General Officer Commanding was appointed on 30 July 2026. It is part of Phase 1 of the new force structure, targeted for completion by September 2026. Formation type has not been publicly disclosed.
mouSigned: Not applicable — a military formation, not a commercial project
mouParties: Federal Government of Nigeria (Presidency and Ministry of Defence); Nigerian Army
mouSignificance: Creation approved by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu on 23 July 2026, announced by Bayo Onanuga. A General Officer Commanding was appointed by the Chief of Army Staff, Lt.-Gen. Waidi Shaibu, on 30 July 2026.

milestones.event: President Tinubu approves creation of the 10 Division headquarters in Jalingo, Taraba State.
Army appoints a General Officer Commanding for 10 Division.
Phase 1 target: division established and operational.

phase: Phase 1 of two (targeted complete by September 2026)
aorNote: Taraba and Adamawa states, separated from the former 7 Division (Maiduguri) area of responsibility.
significance: Brings divisional-level command to the Benue–Mambilla corridor and eases the load on 7 Division in the North-East.

name: 83 Division (Benin City) — new
summary: New divisional HQ approved July 2026 for Edo, Delta and Bayelsa states; Phase 2, due December 2026.
description: 83 Division is a new Nigerian Army divisional headquarters headquartered in Benin City, Edo State, created under the expansion to twelve divisions approved on 23 July 2026. It takes over Edo, Delta and Bayelsa states — the bulk of the former 6 Division (Port Harcourt) area of responsibility in the Niger Delta and the Benin Creek corridor. Unlike the other three new divisions, 83 Division falls in the second phase of implementation and is the latest to be established.
statusDetail: Approved by the President on 23 July 2026 and announced by the Presidency. A General Officer Commanding was appointed on 30 July 2026. It is the only new division in Phase 2 of the restructuring, which also covers further reorganisation of existing formations and is expected to conclude by December 2026. It is therefore the least established of the four.
mouSigned: Not applicable — a military formation, not a commercial project
mouParties: Federal Government of Nigeria (Presidency and Ministry of Defence); Nigerian Army
mouSignificance: Creation approved by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu on 23 July 2026, announced by Bayo Onanuga. A General Officer Commanding was appointed by the Chief of Army Staff on 30 July 2026. Army spokesperson Col. Anele said the new divisions will commence operations immediately upon attaining Initial Operational Capability.

milestones.event: President Tinubu approves creation of the 83 Division headquarters in Benin City, Edo State.
Army appoints a General Officer Commanding for 83 Division; operations to begin on attaining IOC.
Phase 2 target: 83 Division established, with further reorganisation of existing formations complete.

phase: Phase 2 of two (targeted complete by December 2026)
aorNote: Edo, Delta and Bayelsa states, covering the Benin Creek and western Niger Delta, separated from 6 Division (Port Harcourt).
significance: Splits the South-South theatre in two and gives the western Niger Delta and Benin Creek a dedicated divisional headquarters.
